description.sr_latin: Nadimci, komplimenti i poruke za tvoju dragu osobu.
description.en: Pet names, compliments, and sweet messages for your special person.

phrases.context: Your partner walks in after a long day and you want to greet them with the everyday term of endearment.
phrases.notes: 'Dušo' is the vocative of 'duša' = soul; calling someone this says they are your soul. The default, most natural pet name.

phrases.context: You answer the phone to your girlfriend and want to open with a warm, everyday name, not just hello.
phrases.notes: 'Ljubavi' is the vocative of 'ljubav' = love. Stands alone or combines: 'Ljubavi moja.' Used freely, not only in romantic moments.

phrases.context: You're out in public with your girlfriend and want something affectionate but a touch more reserved than 'dušo'.
phrases.notes: 'Draga' = dear (feminine); 'dragi' for a man. The adjective agrees with the person you're addressing, not the speaker.

phrases.context: You're being flirty and cute with your girlfriend and reach for the playful 'babe'-style nickname.
phrases.notes: 'Maco' is the vocative of 'maca' = (female) kitty. Flirty and very common among younger couples.

phrases.context: Your boyfriend or guy you're dating is being adorable and you want a cute, cuddly nickname for him.
phrases.notes: 'Medo' is the diminutive of 'medved' = bear — a teddy bear, not a grizzly. Usually for guys, but not exclusively.

phrases.context: You want to tell your partner they brighten your day, with a warm name Serbs genuinely use.
phrases.notes: 'Sunce' = sun, a neuter noun, so the possessive is 'moje'. Used for partners and kids alike, and never sounds cheesy.

phrases.context: Your partner did something thoughtful and you want a warm, everyday name that parents also use for kids.
phrases.notes: 'Zlato' = gold, a neuter noun, hence 'moje'. Very natural and not over the top in everyday Serbian.

phrases.context: You're having a tender, sincere moment with your partner and want one of the most heartfelt names.
phrases.notes: 'Srce' = heart, neuter, so the possessive is 'moje'. One of the most emotionally loaded pet names, sincere rather than playful.

phrases.context: Your girlfriend just got dressed up for a night out and you want to tell her sincerely how she looks.
phrases.notes: The prefix 'pre-' intensifies: 'lepa' = pretty, 'prelepa' = stunning. 'Prelepa' for a woman, 'prelep' for a man.

phrases.context: Your partner is trying on a new outfit, or just got a haircut, and asks what you think.
phrases.notes: Literally 'it stands nicely on you' — 'ti' is the dative of the person it suits. Works for clothes, hair, glasses, anything.

phrases.context: Your girlfriend walks in looking incredible and you want a high-energy, slangy reaction.
phrases.notes: Literally 'you killed (it)' in the past tense; 'ubila' for a woman, 'ubio' for a man. Slang, but very natural among young people.

phrases.context: Your girlfriend just figured something out cleverly and you want to praise her mind sincerely.
phrases.notes: 'Baš' adds emphasis and sincerity, like 'really' or 'truly'. 'Pametna' for a woman, 'pametan' for a man.

phrases.context: Your girlfriend just cracked you up and you want to tell her how funny she is.
phrases.notes: 'Mnogo' literally means 'a lot' but here works as 'so/very'. 'Smešna' for a woman, 'smešan' for a man.

phrases.context: Your girlfriend just did something kind and you want to tell her she's the best, plainly and warmly.
phrases.notes: The prefix 'naj-' builds superlatives: 'dobar' = good becomes 'najbolji/najbolja' = best. 'Najbolja' for a woman, 'najbolji' for a man.

phrases.context: You're apart from someone you love and want to send the simple, go-to line saying you wish they were here.
phrases.notes: An inverse construction: literally 'you are missing to me', so the person missed is the subject and 'mi' (to me) is dative.

phrases.context: It's the middle of the day, someone crosses your mind, and you want a light, sweet text to send them.
phrases.notes: 'Misliti na' = to think about; the preposition 'na' takes the accusative, so 'ti' becomes 'tebe'. Not heavy, just affectionate.

phrases.en: I can't wait to see you.
phrases.context: You have a date coming up, or haven't seen them in a while, and want to show your excitement.
phrases.notes: 'Jedva čekam' is literally 'I barely wait' — the set phrase for eager anticipation. 'Da te vidim' = to see you.

phrases.context: You're ready to say the big three words to your partner for the first time and mean every bit of it.
phrases.notes: 'Te' is the accusative clitic 'you'. Unlike English, there's no casual 'love ya' — this always carries weight. The ekavian infinitive is 'voleti'; Bosnians use ijekavian 'voljeti'.

phrases.context: Your partner just woke up, or you want the first text they read today to be a warm one.
phrases.notes: 'Jutro' = morning, neuter, so the greeting is 'dobro jutro'. Swap 'sunce' for any other pet name you like.

phrases.context: It's bedtime and you want to send your partner an affectionate goodnight before they sleep.
phrases.notes: 'Laku noć' = lit. 'easy night', the fixed goodnight (accusative 'laku' agrees with feminine 'noć'). Adding 'ljubavi' makes it personal.

phrases.context: You're saying goodnight to someone you're into and want to end on a flirty, playful note.
phrases.notes: 'Sanjaj' is the imperative of 'sanjati' = to dream; 'me' is the accusative clitic. Playful, not desperate.

phrases.context: Your partner is heading to bed tired and you want a caring, protective way to wish them a good rest.
phrases.notes: 'Spavaj' is the imperative of 'spavati' = to sleep; 'lepo' = nicely here works as 'well'. The pet name softens it.

phrases.en: I always have time for you.
phrases.context: Your girlfriend asks if you're too busy to talk, and you want a smooth, genuine reply over text.
phrases.notes: 'Uvek' = always. After 'imam' the amount is partitive, so 'vreme' = time takes the genitive 'vremena'.

phrases.context: Your partner is teasing you or hinting they might cancel, and you want a light, playful guilt trip.
phrases.notes: 'Nemoj da...' is the standard negative command, softer than a bare imperative. 'Rastužiti' = to make sad, with 'me' as the object.

phrases.context: You're being a little cheesy on purpose with your girlfriend and deliver it with a grin.
phrases.notes: Past tense agrees with the doer: 'ukrala' (she), 'ukrao' (he). 'Mi' = from me (dative of disadvantage), 'srce' = heart is the object.

phrases.sr_latin: Srećan sam kad sam s tobom.
phrases.sr_cyrillic: Срећан сам кад сам с тобом.
phrases.en: I'm happy when I'm with you.
phrases.context: You're having a quiet moment together and want to tell your partner plainly how they make you feel.
phrases.notes: 'Srećan' is the masculine form; a woman says 'srećna'. 'S tobom' = with you uses the instrumental 'tobom' after 's/sa'.

variations.sr_latin: Srećna sam kad sam s tobom.
variations.sr_cyrillic: Срећна сам кад сам с тобом.
variations.en: I'm happy when I'm with you.

phrases.context: You're in a real, serious moment with your partner and want to say how much they matter to you.
phrases.notes: 'Značiti' = to mean; 'mi' is the dative 'to me'. Word order keeps the clitic 'mi' in second position. Save it for genuine moments.

phrases.context: You want to tell your partner how into them you are, in a passionate but everyday way.
phrases.notes: 'Luditi' = to go crazy; 'za' here takes the instrumental 'tobom', giving 'crazy after/about you'. Common and lighter than it sounds.

phrases.context: Your partner is stressed or upset and you want to reassure them that you've got their back.
phrases.notes: 'Tu' = here (right by you), warmer than the more distant 'tamo'. 'Za tebe' = for you uses the accusative after 'za'.

phrases.context: Your partner is worried about something tough ahead and you want to calm them and offer hope.
phrases.notes: Future tense: clitic 'će' + infinitive 'biti' = will be. 'U redu' = lit. 'in order', the everyday way to say 'okay'.

phrases.context: Your partner is anxious over something small and you want to gently tell them to let it go.
phrases.notes: 'Ne' + imperative 'brini' negates the command: 'don't worry'. The pet name 'dušo' softens the whole line.

phrases.en: Sorry, I didn't mean it like that.
phrases.context: Something you said came out wrong and hurt your partner, so you walk it back right away.
phrases.notes: 'Izvini' is the informal 'sorry'. Past tense agrees with the speaker: 'mislio' (m), 'mislila' (f); 'nisam mislio' = I didn't mean.

variations.en: Sorry, I didn't mean it like that.

phrases.context: A disagreement with your partner is heating up and you want to defuse it and stay close.
phrases.notes: 'Hajde da...' = let's, forms a suggestion with the present tense. 'Svađati se' = to argue is reflexive, hence 'se'.

phrases.context: After a tense silence with your partner, you want to open up honestly and break the ice.
phrases.notes: 'Mrzim' = I hate; 'kad' = when introduces the clause. 'Svađati se' is reflexive, so 'se' stays with it.
